speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of the rash and when it first appeared relative to your fever and other symptoms? Have you started any new medications or traveled recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash on her trunk and extremities look like small, red spots that are slightly raised, and do they seem to be in different stages of healing? Have you noticed if the rash is more prominent on the face and proximal extremities compared to the distal limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions on her body primarily papular and vesicular, resembling dewdrops on a rose petal? Have you observed any crusting lesions alongside the active blisters?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of a facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, alongside recent low-grade fever and rhinorrhea, is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
